subject: Re: TechSummit - badge scanner export, consent language & CRM mapping
messages:
From: Alex Patel <alex@eventops.co>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@techsummit.org>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: TechSummit - initial badge scanner export + consent language

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for confirming Redwood as a sponsor for TechSummit. Attached is the badge-scanner export spec we use (CSV) and a first-pass consent language we include at registration and on the scanner modal.

Quick summary:
- We can push nightly CSVs (UTC) or provide an SFTP with hourly drops.
- Export columns: badge_id, first_name, last_name, email, company, job_title, opt_in_marketing (yes/no), opt_in_sessions (yes/no), session_ids (pipe-separated), checkin_time
- We ask partners to confirm HubSpot property names and whether to send a separate marketing opt-in event.

Attachments: techsummit-scanner-mapping-v1.csv, consent-language-draft.docx

Questions for Redwood:
1) Do you need a dedupe key beyond email (we can include badge_id and company id)?
2) Is the provided opt_in_marketing language sufficient for your compliance team, or do you need the longer form?
3) Preferred ingestion: nightly CSV or SFTP push?

If you want, I can hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the file.

Best,
Alex Patel
EventOps - Integrations
alex@eventops.co

Subject: Re: TechSummit - initial badge scanner export + consent language

Thanks, Alex. Forwarding to the events and ops crew — Marissa, Ben, Grace, looping you in for mapping and compliance checks.

On your questions:
1) Dedupe: primary key should be email when present; fallback to badge_id when email is missing. We also like a composite of email+company for enterprise accounts.
2) Consent: the short modal is fine for onsite scanning, but our legal team prefers an explicit checkbox property captured in HubSpot (we call it "event_marketing_consent"). Can you include a column that records the exact consent string shown (or a consent_code) so we can reconcile?
3) Ingestion: pref SFTP with hourly drops if possible — supports faster follow-up. Nightly is acceptable if SFTP isn't available.

Operational asks:
- Can you add a stable scanner_id per device in the export (scanner_id) so we can trace source of records?
- Please indicate session_ids as semicolon-separated instead of pipe (we'll handle splitting).

Marissa — can you map the columns to HubSpot property names below and return a CSV? Ben — confirm any SFDC fallback we should care about. Grace — any red flags from privacy?

Connor O'Brien
Head of Field Marketing 
Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TechSummit - badge scanner export + HubSpot mapping (updated)

Hi all,

I pulled Alex's CSV and made an updated mapping with HubSpot property names and a couple of small changes. I attached techsummit-scanner-mapping-v2.csv and a revised consent-language-draft.docx that includes the consent_code column we discussed.

Proposed field mapping (excerpt):
- badge_id -> event_badge_id (text)
- scanner_id -> event_scanner_id (text)
- first_name -> firstname (standard)
- last_name -> lastname (standard)
- email -> email (standard)
- company -> company (standard)
- job_title -> jobtitle (text)
- opt_in_marketing -> event_marketing_consent (boolean: "yes"/"no")
- consent_code -> event_consent_code (text)
- session_ids (semicolon-delimited) -> event_sessions (text multi-value)
- checkin_time -> event_checkin_time (datetime)

Notes / decisions:
- We'll set email as the primary dedupe key; where email is missing, we use event_badge_id.
- event_marketing_consent will be written as true/false into HubSpot and we will also send a custom "event_consent_timestamp" if provided.
- For enterprise accounts we will set "company_account_id" when present to help SFDC match.

Attachments: techsummit-scanner-mapping-v2.csv (includes the header-to-property mapping), consent-language-draft.docx (adds the consent_code and explicit checkbox wording).

Open items for Alex / TechSummit:
- Confirm SFTP details and hourly drop cadence (preferred).
- Can you provide the scanner firmware ID that will populate scanner_id? We need a stable value per device.
- Do you want Redwood to only ingest records with event_marketing_consent == yes for marketing workflows, or do you want us to ingest all and tag policy for downstream cadence?

Ben, Grace — flag anything else. If we get confirmation today/tomorrow we can run a dry ingest to our staging HubSpot instance and report back.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Field Ops Lead, Events
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Hi everyone,

Thanks for the quick turnaround — the updated mapping looks good. A few confirmations from the organizer side:

1) We will provide SFTP details (host + user + key) by end of day Thursday; hourly drops are available.
2) scanner_id will be the device serial number (firmware stable). We'll include that in v2 exports.
3) We prefer partners ingest all records and use the event_marketing_consent flag to gate marketing sends (so we recommend ingest+tagging rather than filter-out).

I've also uploaded an approved short consent string to the shared drive and started a DocuSign powerform to get the data-sharing amendment signed (link below). Please confirm who's signing on Redwood's side so we can route the envelope.
